about: Table that lets DOEFF002 separate "attributes that a base class (outside the repo) owns itself" from "attributes that the class places itself" (rules::class_inheritance). Names are the full spelling resolved from imports (the App in `from textual.app import App` is `textual.app.App`).
transparent_bases_about: Bases known to have no instance attributes at all. A class whose only bases are these is read the same as a class with no base attributes (and, as for a class with no base, it is reported for attributes first assigned outside init).
framework_attributes_about: Attributes known to be owned by the base (not all of the base's attributes -- even when listed, the base is read as possibly having other attributes). The framework expects subclasses to write to these names (Textual's `self.sub_title = ...` changes the header display), so renaming them to `_mut_` would break it. Even when a subclass also places them in `__init__`, they are not reported as writes to a base attribute. Only entries are listed for which the framework's source was checked to declare the name in the base class and to document it as an interface for users to write.
